# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

1505	/// The prompt a task was sent as: the compiled markdown the harness received,
1506	/// or the text as typed until it compiles. Its links to files open them.
1507	fn task_prompt(ix: usize, task: &PromptTask, open: &OpenFile, cx: &App) -> AnyElement {
1508	    match &task.compiled {
1509	        Some(compiled) => {
1510	            let prompt = div()
1511	                .id(("compiled-prompt", ix))
1512	                .min_w_0()
1513	                .child(markdown_view(
1514	                    ("prompt", ix),
1515	                    &compiled.markdown,
1516	                    Some(open),
1517	                    cx,
1518	                ));
1519	            // Lets UI tests find the compiled prompt; inert in normal builds.
1520	            gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(prompt).into_any_element()
1521	        }
1522	        None => div()
1523	            .min_w_0()
1524	            .text_color(cx.theme().muted_foreground)
1525	            .child(task.text.clone())
1526	            .into_any_element(),
1527	    }
1528	}
1529	
1530	/// A task in the expanded list, on one line: its title, then the start of its
1531	/// prompt as typed.
1532	fn task_summary(ix: usize, task: &PromptTask, cx: &App) -> AnyElement {
1533	    let first_line: SharedString = task
1534	        .text
1535	        .lines()
1536	        .find(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
1537	        .unwrap_or_default()
1538	        .to_string()
1539	        .into();
1540	    let summary = h_flex()
1541	        .id(("history-task", ix))
1542	        .flex_1()
1543	        .min_w_0()
1544	        .gap_3()
1545	        .child(div().flex_none().child(task_title(ix, task, cx)))
1546	        .child(div().flex_1().min_w_0().truncate().child(first_line));
1547	    // Lets UI tests find the task; inert in normal builds.
1548	    gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(summary).into_any_element()
1549	}
1550	
1551	/// A task's output as a table: a row for each piece of text, tool call and
1552	/// error, in order, with its kind as a badge, what it was, and a tool call's
1553	/// state spelled out rather than only coloured. While the reply streams, its
1554	/// last row shows the harness's latest raw output in place of what is not yet
1555	/// known of it. With `open`, files
1556	/// the output links to, and those its file tools worked on, open when clicked.
1557	pub(crate) fn output_table(
1558	    task_ix: usize,
1559	    reply: &Reply,
1560	    open: Option<&OpenFile>,
1561	    cx: &App,
1562	) -> AnyElement {
1563	    let theme = cx.theme();
1564	    let rows = reply.rows();
1565	    // An unfinished reply always has a row, so only a finished one is empty.
1566	    if rows.is_empty() {
1567	        return div()
1568	            .text_color(theme.muted_foreground)
1569	            .child("No output.")
1570	            .into_any_element();
1571	    }
1572	
1573	    let header = TableHeader::new().child(
1574	        TableRow::new()
1575	            .child(TableHead::new().w(KIND_WIDTH).flex_none().child("Type"))
1576	            .child(TableHead::new().flex_1().min_w_0().child("Output"))
1577	            .child(TableHead::new().w(STATUS_WIDTH).flex_none().child("Status")),
1578	    );
1579	    let project_dir = ProjectDirectory::get(cx);
1580	    let body = TableBody::new().children(rows.iter().enumerate().map(|(row_ix, row)| {
1581	        let detail = match row {
1582	            OutputRow::Text(text) if text.trim().is_empty() => raw_tail(reply, cx),
1583	            OutputRow::Pending => raw_tail(reply, cx),
1584	            OutputRow::Text(text) => div()
1585	                .w_full()
1586	                .min_w_0()
1587	                .child(markdown_view(
1588	                    ElementId::NamedInteger(format!("output-text-{task_ix}").into(), row_ix as u64),
1589	                    text,
1590	                    open,
1591	                    cx,
1592	                ))
1593	                .into_any_element(),
1594	            OutputRow::Tool(call) => {
1595	                let summary = call
1596	                    .summary
1597	                    .as_deref()
1598	                    .map(|summary| relative_to_project(summary, project_dir.as_deref()));
1599	                match summary {
1600	                    // A command is laid out across lines and highlighted, so it
1601	                    // can be read rather than cut off.
1602	                    Some(command) if ToolKind::of(&call.name) == ToolKind::Command => div()
1603	                        .w_full()
1604	                        .min_w_0()
1605	                        .child(TextView::markdown(
1606	                            ElementId::NamedInteger(
1607	                                format!("output-command-{task_ix}").into(),
1608	                                row_ix as u64,
1609	                            ),
1610	                            code_block("bash", &shell_format::format_command(&command)),
1611	                        ))
1612	                        .into_any_element(),
1613	                    summary => h_flex()
1614	                        .w_full()
1615	                        .min_w_0()
1616	                        .gap_2()
1617	                        .when_some(call.shown_name(), |row, name| {
1618	                            row.child(div().flex_none().font_medium().child(name.to_string()))
1619	                        })
1620	                        // Its input is on its way.
1621	                        .when(row.is_partial(), |row| {
1622	                            row.child(div().flex_1().min_w_0().child(raw_tail(reply, cx)))
1623	                        })
1624	                        .when_some(summary, |row, summary| {
1625	                            let text = div()
1626	                                .min_w_0()
1627	                                .truncate()
1628	                                .font_family(theme.mono_font_family.clone())
1629	                                .child(summary);
1630	                            // A file a file tool worked on opens when clicked.
1631	                            let file = open
1632	                                .filter(|_| call.works_on_a_file())
1633	                                .zip(call.summary.clone());
1634	                            match file {
1635	                                Some((open, target)) => {
1636	                                    let open = open.clone();
1637	                                    let link = text
1638	                                        .id(("output-file", row_ix))
1639	                                        .text_color(theme.link)
1640	                                        .cursor_pointer()
1641	                                        .hover(|style| style.underline())
1642	                                        .on_click(move |_, window, cx| {
1643	                                            file_link::open_link(&target, &open, window, cx)
1644	                                        });
1645	                                    // Lets UI tests find the link; inert in normal builds.
1646	                                    row.child(gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(link))
1647	                                }
1648	                                None => row.child(text),
1649	                            }
1650	                        })
1651	                        .into_any_element(),
1652	                }
1653	            }
1654	            OutputRow::Error(error) => div()
1655	                .min_w_0()
1656	                .text_color(theme.foreground)
1657	                .child(error.to_string())
1658	                .into_any_element(),
1659	        };
1660	        let detail = div()
1661	            .id(("output-row", row_ix))
1662	            .w_full()
1663	            .min_w_0()
1664	            .child(detail);
1665	
1666	        let status = match row {
1667	            OutputRow::Tool(call) => {
1668	                let icon = match call.state {
1669	                    ToolState::Running => Spinner::new().small().into_any_element(),
1670	                    ToolState::Done => Icon::new(IconName::Check)
1671	                        .small()
1672	                        .text_color(theme.success)
1673	                        .into_any_element(),
1674	                    ToolState::Failed => Icon::new(IconName::X)
1675	                        .small()
1676	                        .text_color(theme.danger)
1677	                        .into_any_element(),
1678	                };
1679	                Some(
1680	                    h_flex().gap_1p5().child(icon).child(
1681	                        div()
1682	                            .map(|state| match call.state {
1683	                                // A failure reads at full strength.
1684	                                ToolState::Failed => state.font_medium(),
1685	                                _ => state.text_color(theme.muted_foreground),
1686	                            })
1687	                            .child(call.state.label()),
1688	                    ),
1689	                )
1690	            }
1691	            OutputRow::Text(_) | OutputRow::Error(_) | OutputRow::Pending => None,
1692	        };
1693	
1694	        TableRow::new()
1695	            .child(
1696	                TableCell::new()
1697	                    .w(KIND_WIDTH)
1698	                    .flex_none()
1699	                    .items_start()

content.text:
Syntax highlighting is in: the live raw-output preview in the message list now shows each JSON line in colour. For tool calls of a known type, the JSON is replaced with a short placeholder until the call's input arrives. The prompt-mode tests pass, including two new ones. I haven't launched the app to look at it on screen.

**Highlighting.** The kit's built-in JSON grammar colours each of the last three raw lines. A line cut off partway through an object still gets coloured as far as it goes. No new dependency was needed.

**Placeholders.** I used the tool-type list already in `src/prompt_mode.rs` (the one behind the Files / Edit / Command / Web / Agent badges). While one of those calls has no input yet, the row shows a muted line and a skeleton bar instead of the JSON:

| Type | Tools | Placeholder |
|---|---|---|
| Files | Read, Glob, Grep, LS, NotebookRead | "Choosing what to read…" |
| Edit | Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit | "Writing the edit…" |
| Command | Bash, BashOutput, KillShell, KillBash | "Writing the command…" |
| Web | WebFetch, WebSearch | "Preparing the request…" |
| Agent | Task, Agent | "Briefing the agent…" |

Once the input arrives, the placeholder is replaced by what the row normally shows: the formatted command for commands, the file path or argument for the others. The placeholder takes up the same height as the preview it replaces, so rows don't jump. Any other tool, such as MCP tools, still shows the highlighted JSON. So does the row at the end for whatever the harness does next.

**Tests.** The full suite ran 81 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `palette::tests::lists_files_by_path_leaving_out_ignored_ones`, which expects `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` in the file list but doesn't get it. That's in the palette's file listing, which I didn't touch.
